brief.user_goal: Build a polished single-page local volunteer signup interface. Provide a labeled Name input (name), Email input (email), submit control (submit), and status (form-status). An empty submission must visibly say Required. After filling a name and valid email, submission must say Confirmed. Implement local validation with noValidate so an empty submission reaches the handler. Label it a demo, not a real booking. Parentheses specify required data-testid values.
audience: people using this service on desktop and mobile

interactions.action: Provide a labeled Name input (name), Email input (email), submit control (submit), and status (form-status). An empty submission must visibly say Required. After filling a name and valid email, submission must say Confirmed. Implement local validation with noValidate so an empty submission reaches the handler. Label it a demo, not a real booking.
interactions.expected: All specified state transitions work using local demonstration data.

acceptance_criteria: No serious or critical automated accessibility violations

interpretations.meaning_in_context: Introduces light, approachable energy without sacrificing clarity or professionalism; manifests in subtle visual cues like rounded corners, animated transitions, or whimsical iconography, but not in a childish or distracting way.

decisions.choice: rounded corners on input fields and form controls
decisions.rationale: Rounded shapes contribute to a playful yet approachable feel, aligning with the 'playful' descriptor while maintaining a clean, modern aesthetic similar to Linear or Stripe.

decisions.choice: subtle hover animations on interactive elements (e.g., submit button)
decisions.rationale: Playful does not mean chaotic; gentle micro-interactions enhance engagement without overwhelming the user or disrupting the form's clarity.

interpretations.meaning_in_context: Emphasizes structured, precise forms with clean lines and aligned components, reinforcing clarity and consistency in layout and spacing.

decisions.choice: grid-based alignment with consistent spacing and aligned form fields
decisions.rationale: Geometric design ensures predictable, scalable structure across devices, supporting usability and visual harmony in a form-heavy interface.

decisions.choice: medium spacing between form fields and sections
decisions.rationale: Medium density supports readability and prevents visual clutter, allowing geometric precision to shine without sacrificing comfort.

interpretations.meaning_in_context: Uses intentional, non-distracting color to highlight states (e.g., required, confirmed) and guide user attention, without overwhelming the interface.

decisions.choice: use a single accent color (e.g., teal or indigo) for the submit button and status indicators
decisions.rationale: Colorful is used to signal state changes (Required → Confirmed) in a clear, visible way, supporting the form's feedback loop while staying within a clean, professional tone.

decisions.choice: highlight required fields in a soft red or orange border when empty
decisions.rationale: Color is used to communicate validation states, improving usability and aligning with the playful yet functional tone of the interface.

interpretations.source_quote: Clean product UI, like Linear or Stripe
interpretations.meaning_in_context: Prioritizes clarity, minimalism, and consistent control design—no decorative elements or visual noise—ensuring the form remains focused on user action and data entry.

decisions.choice: remove all decorative graphics or illustrations
decisions.rationale: A clean product UI emphasizes function over ornamentation; this ensures the form remains focused on the core task of signing up.

decisions.choice: use clear, sans-serif typefaces with consistent font weights and hierarchy
decisions.rationale: Clean UI relies on legible, well-structured typography to support fast reading and accurate data entry.

ux_priorities: No serious or critical automated accessibility violations
assumptions: Users will enter valid email formats when prompted (no email validation beyond basic format)
The form will be used primarily in a browser environment with standard touch and keyboard input
The 'demo' label will be clearly visible and not misleading to users

brief.user_goal: Build a polished single-page independent film production checklist interface. Provide a task called Prepare materials, a toggle control (task-toggle), and a text status (task-status), initially Pending. Activating the control changes it to Completed; activating again restores Pending. Parentheses specify required data-testid values.
audience: people using this service on desktop and mobile

interactions.action: Provide a task called Prepare materials, a toggle control (task-toggle), and a text status (task-status), initially Pending. Activating the control changes it to Completed; activating again restores Pending.
interactions.expected: All specified state transitions work using local demonstration data.

acceptance_criteria: No serious or critical automated accessibility violations

interpretations.meaning_in_context: A welcoming, approachable tone in color and texture, without being overly decorative or bright; supports a friendly yet professional feel suitable for creative workflows.

decisions.choice: neutral with subtle warm undertones (e.g., soft beige, warm gray)
decisions.rationale: The 'warm' descriptor suggests a friendly, inviting tone that aligns with creative professionals, while maintaining professionalism. Avoiding saturated or bold colors ensures clarity and focus on task state.

interpretations.meaning_in_context: Deliberate, structured presentation of information with clear hierarchy and readable flow, emphasizing clarity and purpose over visual noise.

decisions.choice: editorial
decisions.rationale: The editorial style ensures a clear, readable hierarchy and consistent information flow, which is essential for a checklist interface where users need to track progress efficiently.

decisions.choice: focus
decisions.rationale: A focused layout emphasizes the single task (Prepare materials) with minimal distractions, supporting the editorial intent of clarity and purpose.

interpretations.meaning_in_context: A sense of physicality or touch in the interface—suggesting a human, hands-on experience, such as a physical checklist being flipped or marked.

decisions.choice: toggle with a clear visual state change (e.g., checkmark or solid fill on completion)
decisions.rationale: The tactile quality is best expressed through a physical-like toggle that provides immediate visual feedback when activated, mimicking the feel of marking a task completed.

decisions.choice: moderate padding around controls to create a sense of physical separation
decisions.rationale: Tactile design benefits from intentional spacing that gives the interface a grounded, physical presence, enhancing user confidence in task management.

interpretations.source_quote: Clean product UI, like Linear or Stripe
interpretations.meaning_in_context: A minimalist, uncluttered interface with clear visual hierarchy and functional clarity, avoiding unnecessary elements or visual complexity.

decisions.choice: focus
decisions.rationale: A focused layout with minimal decorative elements aligns with the clean product UI standard, ensuring the task and its status are the primary focus.

decisions.choice: low
decisions.rationale: The specified 'low' density directly supports a clean, uncluttered interface, reducing visual noise and improving readability across devices.

intent.primary_action: Toggle 'Prepare materials' to mark as completed or pending
ux_priorities: All specified state transitions work using local demonstration data
No serious or critical automated accessibility violations
assumptions: Users are familiar with toggle-based task management in checklists.
The interface will be used in a quiet, focused environment (e.g., pre-production planning).
The 'local demonstration only' constraint means no external data sources or integrations are required.
